author: Unreal Engine
description: Join us as Etienne Carrier guides us through a breakdown of the Mesh Terrain level presented at the State of Unreal 2026. We will break down what Mesh Terrain is, how it can be used, and explore how this scene was set up and which modifiers and assets were used to achieve this result.
title: A Practical Look at Mesh Terrain | Inside Unreal

author: Unreal Engine
description:
Live service games require an efficient content pipeline to continuously deliver updates to players, and generally development of new seasonal content and features has to happen simultaneously for multiple releases at once. 

Unreal Engine’s modular gameplay features and Game Feature Plugins (GFPs) map nicely to this problem, enforcing a good content structure and allowing for unrelated features for different releases to be safely built on a single game branch. 

However, there’s a large gap between what UE offers out of the box and what game production practically needs. 

In this talk recorded at Unreal Fest Chicago 2026, Riot Games start by exploring Game Feature Plugins and how they function in some detail, talking about their advantages and their flexibility. 

They also cover some of the plugins’ weaknesses and common misconceptions. The team then dives into "Build Recipes", a Riot-built data-driven UE system to manipulate the blend of GFPs that constitute a given released versi
title: Game Feature Plugins for Live Service Games at Riot | Unreal Fest Chicago 2026

description:
